output.question: Has Paramount announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. Paramount announced layoffs in February 2024, when CEO Bob Bakish told employees that the company would reduce its workforce; reporting at the time put the affected number at about 800 employees. More recently, after Paramount/Skydance's 2026 merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, Skydance's leaders told employees that integration would involve difficult workforce decisions, and Paramount Skydance began a voluntary buyout program ahead of further layoffs; the company had not disclosed the total number of expected cuts as of October 26, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Paramount Global announced workforce reductions in February 2024; sources familiar with the matter told CNN that approximately 800 employees, or about 3% of the workforce, would be affected.

On October 6, 2026, leaders of the newly combined Skydance company—which brought Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery together—said that integrating the companies would involve difficult decisions affecting the workforce, with layoffs expected as part of the cost-savings effort.

On October 26, 2026, Skydance announced a voluntary buyout program for eligible employees and said layoffs were part of its planned cost reductions, but it had not revealed the extent of the job cuts.

passages.quote: The company's chief executive, Bob Bakish, announced the layoffs in a memo to employees Tuesday obtained by CNN.
Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce
To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program.
The company has not revealed at this point the extent of the job cuts it expects.

caveats: The most recent 2026 announcements were made under Skydance/Paramount's post-merger structure, so they describe the combined company rather than only the legacy Paramount workforce.
The 2026 sources confirm planned workforce reductions and a voluntary buyout program but do not provide a final total number of layoffs.
The approximately 800 figure from 2024 was reported by sources familiar with the situation; Paramount's CEO memo did not specify a number.
